facts.fact: The World Bank's appraisal document states that the civil registration system is outdated and still records on paper the ten acts of a person's life (birth, death and marriage among them); no date is given for the statement, so the document's publication date is used.

The World Bank says that in the urban areas of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire digitalisation remains uneven across the civil registration centres, and that offices' access to broadband is uneven; it gives no count of offices or centres, and no date, so the document's publication date is used.

The World Bank describes the civil registration system as decentralised, operated by municipal officials and overseen by the Ministry of Territorial Administration, Decentralization and Local Development, with the justice and health ministries also involved; no date is given, so the document's publication date is used.

Sub-component 3.1 of the Congo Digital Acceleration Project, an IBRD loan of US$100 million appraised on 11 May 2022, allots US$11 million to modernising civil registration and the prerequisites of a digital ID: a technical assessment, an operational plan, a legal review, equipment to digitalise registration posts and a secure civil registration database; no domestic budget line is stated.

systems.owner: municipal officials, overseen by the Ministry of Territorial Administration, Decentralization and Local Development, with the Ministry of Justice and the ministry in charge of health and population
systems.tiers: decentralised civil registration centres; paper records; digitalisation uneven across centres in urban Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire
planned: equipment for the digitalisation of CR registration posts and a secure database for record retrieval and data exchange

systems.owner: National Police, overseen by the Ministry of Security and Public Order

systems.tiers: planned: the project funds only the prerequisites; deployment is left to a future project
planned: online requests for civil registration records and other certificates, with in-person access points through the postal network (SOPECO)
